payload.title: Thinking
payload.text:
I'm setting up three subagents to run in parallel, one for each file, with each one limited to fixing only its own file. I'll hold off on running anything myself until they finish, then run npm test and report back in one line. Each subagent gets its file path, the bug, and the rule not to touch tests or other files.

I'm weighing whether the subagents should be allowed to read and run tests, since they might hit failures outside their own files. I'll let them read the tests but not edit them, and keep each one's scope narrow. I'm also settling on the working directory: the user wrote /tmp/vcmp/w/t2, which is the same place as the symlinked path, so I'll use that one.

payload.prompt:
Project: /tmp/vcmp/w/t2 (a Node project; `npm test` runs node:test). Three tests currently fail, and there is exactly one bug in each of src/pricing.ts, src/inventory.ts and src/checkout.ts. Other agents are fixing the other two files in parallel.

Your job: find and fix the single bug in **src/pricing.ts only**. The doc comments in that file describe the intended behavior; treat them as the spec. Read the relevant tests (read-only) to confirm the expected behavior.

Rules:
- Edit only src/pricing.ts. Do not edit any test file or any other file.
- Make the minimal fix for the one bug. Do not refactor or reformat unrelated code.
- You may read files freely. Do not run `npm test` in a way that changes files; running it to observe failures is fine but not required.
- When finished, reply with a short report: the bug you found, the line(s) you changed, and why it matches the doc comment.

The `inStock` test was already passing and I did not touch it.

I did not run `npm test`. No other files were edited.

**Bug:** In `checkout`, the reservation loop was `if (!reserve(sku, qty)) { continue; }`. When `reserve` returned `false` (not enough stock), the code skipped that SKU and carried on. The doc comment says `checkout` should throw `'out of stock <sku>'` in that case.

**Change (line 6):**
```ts
if (!reserve(sku, qty)) { throw new Error(`out of stock ${sku}`); }
```

**Why it matches the spec:** `reserve` in `src/inventory.ts` returns `false` when it cannot take `qty` units, so the new line throws with the SKU in the message. The test `checkout throws when out of stock` in `test/checkout.test.ts` expects `/out of stock B2/` for a SKU with zero stock, which this now satisfies. I did not run `npm test`. I did not touch any other file.
